concerns.text: T060 requires prs_labeled.csv to contain the full pr_schema columns (comment_count, time_to_merge_minutes, review_cycles, complexity_score, loc, hour_of_day, day_of_week) and validates row-by-row with pydantic, but those values are only computed downstream by T061 (complexity/loc) and T062 (metrics/temporal). As written, T060 cannot produce a schema-valid file — the implementer has no defined source for those columns at T060 time. Either T060 must write only label columns (with a reduced contract) or T061/T062 must write the full-schema file; the current task set is unexecutable as ordered.

T063 requires results.json to include effect-size interpretation and sensitivity-comparison sections, and T065 extends it with complexity_correlation and gate status — but statistical_result.schema.yaml sets additionalProperties: false. The aggregated results.json as specified will fail its own declared schema validation, so the verification ('conforming to statistical_result.schema.yaml') can never pass. The task must either name a separate aggregated-results schema or restrict the schema-validated portion.

T064 writes data/audit/audit_log.jsonl, manual_audit_results.json, error_rate.json, while the data model specifies data/processed/audit_log.csv with the AuditSample entity (predicted_label, human_ground_truth, correct, notes). The audit output has no single agreed contract; the implementer cannot satisfy both. Pick one location/format and update the data model or the task.

T068's verification 'a fresh clone following quickstart.md reproduces all artifacts' is not deterministically executable: the pipeline depends on live GitHub API responses (changing PR data) and T064 requires interactive human input (which by T064's own spec may exit non-zero). Define a concrete, checkable verification instead — e.g., a scripted run with recorded exit statuses, artifact existence + schema checks, and a documented human-audit step — rather than an unverifiable 'fresh clone reproduces' claim.

T015a/T015c and T047/T053 are marked [X] (complete), but the re-plan note states the prior round failed because data artifacts were never produced, and no evidence of these completions (files, test results) is cited. Completed-task claims require actual evidence; either cite the existing artifacts/tests or re-open these tasks like the other rejected ones.

T060's verification says 'python code/data/run_pipeline.py exits 0', but the same driver is the entry point for a chain whose later stages (T064 human audit) can legitimately fail. Clarify that exit-0 applies to the T060 stage only (fetch+classify+write prs_labeled.csv), so the implementer knows the exact success criterion at this task's boundary.
